name: Question 18
problem:
The position vector $r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ relative to a fixed origin $O$ at time $t$ seconds is given by

$$
r=⟨5{t}^{3}-2{t}^{2}+3,\,{t}^{4}-3{t}^{2}+1⟩.
$$

Calculate the magnitude of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=2\,\text{s}.$ Do not round the answer.

The magnitude of the acceleration is
{{field-1}}
${\text{m/s}}^{2}$
worked_solution:
To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do by differentiating the position vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(5{t}^{3}-2{t}^{2}+3),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{4}-3{t}^{2}+1)⟩ \\  & =⟨15{t}^{2}-4t,\,4{t}^{3}-6t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t} \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}t},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}t}⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(15{t}^{2}-4t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4{t}^{3}-6t)⟩ \\  & =⟨30t-4,\,12{t}^{2}-6⟩\end{aligned}
$$

To find the acceleration at time $t=2,$ we substitute $t=2$ into the above:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(2) & =⟨30(2)-4,\,12(2)^{2}-6⟩ \\  & =⟨60-4,\,48-6⟩ \\  & =⟨56,\,42⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute $|a(2)|:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|a(2)| & =|⟨56,\,42⟩| \\  & =\sqrt{{56}^{2}+{42}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{3136+1764} \\  & =\sqrt{4900} \\  & =70\end{aligned}
$$

So, the magnitude of the acceleration at time $t=2\,\text{s}$ is $70{\text{ m/s}}^{2}.$

EXPLANATION

To compute the acceleration vector, we need to differentiate the velocity vector. So first, we need to compute the velocity vector, which we can do by differentiating the position vector: v=drdt=⟨dxdt,dydt⟩=⟨ddt(5t3−2t2+3),ddt(t4−3t2+1)⟩=⟨15t2−4t,4t3−6t⟩

Now, to compute the acceleration vector, we differentiate the velocity vector: a=dvdt=⟨dudt,dvdt⟩=⟨ddt(15t2−4t),ddt(4t3−6t)⟩=⟨30t−4,12t2−6⟩

To find the acceleration at time t=2, we substitute t=2 into the above: a(2)=⟨30(2)−4,12(2)2−6⟩=⟨60−4,48−6⟩=⟨56,42⟩

Finally, to find the magnitude of the acceleration, we compute |a(2)|: |a(2)|=|⟨56,42⟩|=562+422=3136+1764=4900=70

So, the magnitude of the acceleration at time t=2s is 70 m/s2.
